title: Sales partnership scratch notes - AcmeAI research & outbound
content:
Account: AcmeAI (mid-market, generative search product)

Quick context/why they matter:
- Recently raised Series B (~$60M) per press release (Dec 2023) — investing in product to scale.
- Headcount ~120, growing ML and infra teams.
- Public job posts: ML infra engineer, infra reliability (signals they run their own clusters).
- Use case alignment: product is latency-sensitive search + contextual generation — good fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private.

Key contacts (from LinkedIn / company site):
- Priya Mehta — Head of ML (founder-adjacent, previously at BigSearch) — primary champion target.
- Mark Ellis — VP Eng (infra ownership) — technical/compliance questions.
- Sarah Lopez — Product Manager, search relevance — cares about quality/regressions.

Tech signals / infra hints:
- Mentions of Kubernetes + custom in-house serving in Eng blog (2023).
- Likely using mixed GPU fleet (some clouds + on-prem for cost) — our Private or Dedicated messaging resonates.
- Concern: current stack struggles with latency spikes during peak traffic and cost per token.

Pain points we should highlight:
- Unpredictable latency on peak queries — affects UX conversions.
- Rising inference spend as they scale (token costs + engineering ops).
- Model rollouts/regression risk — need safe canarying + monitoring.

Value props (tailored):
- Predictable latency & autoscaling (Dedicated pools) to avoid tail latency during peaks.
- Cost controls: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization suggestions to reduce per-token cost.
- Safe rollouts: canary/A-B and immediate fallback to smaller model variants to avoid quality regressions.
- Private deployment (VPC) for compliance and hybrid infra support — integrate with their existing KMS.

Quick outbound sequences (email ideas + CTAs)
1) Short cold email (subject variants):
- Subject: "Reduce inference costs and tail latency at AcmeAI"
- Body (short): "Priya — congrats on the recent funding. Quick note: we help teams like yours cut per-token cost by 20–50% and eliminate tail latency with dedicated inference pools + smart caching. Any chance for a 20-min call next week to share a few performance numbers we found for similar search apps? 
 — Aisha"

2) Follow-up (value add):
- "Sharing a short excerpt from a recent case: fintech startup cut 35% token spend via batching + KV cache. Happy to run a quick, no-commit perf estimate on a sample prompt."

3) Call script (first intro, 20 mins):
- 0-3m: quick intros, confirm priorities (latency vs cost vs security).
- 3-8m: ask about traffic patterns, peak QPS, current model types, deployment modes (cloud/private), SLOs.
- 8-14m: surface Redwood approaches: Dedicated pools, prefix/KV caching, quantization profiles, routing/fallbacks.
- 14-18m: quick probe on rollout processes — how they test for quality regressions.
- 18-20m: agree next steps (POC vs perf estimate), ask for sample prompt(s) + cost targets.

Objection handling (common + suggested responses):
- "We already have infra and ops for inference" => A: "Totally — many teams own infra but still struggle with predictable latency and ops overhead. Redwood can run as Dedicated or Private and integrates with your tooling, so we often work alongside infra teams to reduce toil and unit costs without ripping out existing investments."
- "Concerned about vendor lock-in / security" => A: "We offer Private deployments and VPC-controlled control plane with KMS/HSM integrations. Also provide clear export paths and model version pinning so you keep control."
- "Pricing is unclear / worried about cost" => A: "We typically start with a perf + cost estimate on sample prompts. For Dedicated we can propose committed capacity with predictable unit economics. Also our Optimize tooling gives concrete batching/quantization suggestions tied to your workload."
- "Quality/regressions risk from changing model/config" => A: "We provide canary rollouts, prompt-set-backed regression alerts, and the ability to automatically fallback to previous model variants if we detect drop in quality."

Potential POC approach (low friction):
- Start with a 2-week perf & cost estimate: they share 5–10 representative prompts and traffic profile; we run an offline estimate + small-scale Dedicated trial (or hosted sample) to show token costs & latency improvements.
- Deliverables: latency/cost delta report, suggested quantization/config, simple SLO dashboard snapshot.

Notes / TODOs:
- Find internal case study with similar search product (ask Jordan).
- Get an intro to Priya Mehta (ask Jordan/BD).
- Prepare a 2-page one-pager for Dedicated vs Private comparison for AcmeAI that highlights integration points (KMS, network, rollout).
- Draft targeted LinkedIn message and SRE-friendly one-pager for Mark Ellis (focus on ops integration and runbook).

Scratch outbound variants (shorter):
- "Hi Priya — saw AcmeAI's Series B — congrats. We help teams cut inference cost and avoid tail latency with Dedicated inference pools. Quick 15-min chat?"
- "Priya — could I send a 1-page perf sketch for AcmeAI? If it's useful we can do a quick sample run on your prompts."

Open questions to resolve in next sync:
- Do they use on-prem GPUs anywhere? (job posts suggest hybrid)
- Typical sequence lengths and top-k usage for their search product — needed for cost estimation.
- Current monitoring/alerting around model-quality regressions.

Timestamped notes:
- 2024-02-14: initial research + contact list compiled.
- 2024-02-16: Jordan suggested reaching out to Priya via mutual contact from BigSearch alum.
- 2024-02-20: updated outbound sequence and POC approach; flagged internal case study request.

End of scratch notes.

(Notes intentionally informal — borderline bullety; save final one-pager in shared_drives/go-to-market when approved.)
